title: Multiples, HCF and LCM
transcript: The highest common factor is the largest number that divides both quantities. The lowest common multiple is the first positive number they both divide into. Listen for the job: equal grouping uses a common factor, and meeting schedules use a common multiple.

In AMC practice, identical packs or repeating events can signal a common factor or multiple. Write what each clue requires the answer to divide. A Rossmoyne style problem can give the H C F and L C M as clues to find the original pair.
Two activities restart every six minutes and every nine minutes. They start together at time zero. After the start, how many minutes until they first start together again?
The first schedule goes six, twelve and eighteen. The second goes nine and eighteen. They first match at eighteen minutes. That is the least positive number divisible by both periods.

A kit has twenty-four red markers and thirty-six blue markers. Make as many identical packs as possible with none left over. How many packs can you make? Find a number of packs that divides both totals.

The pack count divides both twenty-four and thirty-six. It also divides their difference, which is twelve. Both totals are multiples of twelve. Since the difference is twelve, no larger count can divide both. Make twelve packs. Each contains two reds and three blues.

Two positive integers have highest common factor six and lowest common multiple one hundred and eighty. Find the pair whose difference is as small as possible. Start by dividing each number by their common factor.

Divide both by six. The new pair is coprime, meaning it shares no prime factors. Its lowest common multiple is thirty. Coprime numbers have lowest common multiple equal to their product, so the two scaled values multiply to thirty. List the factor pairs. The closest legal scaled pair is five and six. Their difference is one, smaller than that of the other pairs.

Scale by six to recover thirty and thirty-six. Their gap is six. Multiplying all gaps by the same positive number keeps their order. Their common factor is six, and their least common multiple is one hundred and eighty. These are the two original clues.

The answer to an equal packing problem divides the totals. A repeat time has to be a multiple of both periods. After scaling by the full common factor, make sure the residual pair is coprime. A shared prime would make the common factor larger.
Write what has to divide what. Find the factor or multiple that satisfies that direction. For an unknown pair, remove the greatest common factor first. Multiply back and verify both conditions.
